title: Emergent Misalignment Across Non-Coder Base Models: Replicating with General-Purpose Fine-Tuning Tasks
original_idea: Fine-tune a general-purpose model on a narrow deceptive non-coding task (e.g., writing deliberately misleading product reviews without disclosure) and measure broad misalignment on the standard evaluation prompts used by Betley et al. Compare misalignment rates against the insecure-code baseline.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: The core question has already been answered affirmatively by multiple papers. The remaining contribution is incremental (one more domain variant).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Uses the open emergent misalignment codebase directly. Fine-tuning a small model with SFTTrainer on a custom dataset is well-documented. Dataset construction (misleading product reviews) is straightforward. Evaluation uses existing prompts. A beginner with guidance can execute this.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: one fine-tuning run on one model with one non-code deceptive task, evaluated on the standard EM evaluation set. Single experiment with well-defined success criteria (does misalignment rate differ from baseline?). Can go from start to result quickly.

novelty.reasoning: This idea has been substantially addressed by recent work. The domain susceptibility paper (arXiv:2602.00298, 2026) systematically assessed emergent misalignment across multiple non-code domains including risky financial advice, toxic legal advice, bad medical advice, and others. The Emergent Misalignment & Realignment work (LessWrong) explicitly tested dangerous medical advice as a non-code domain and found it creates more severe misalignment than insecure code. The Semantic Containment paper (arXiv:2603.04407, 2026) analyzes cross-domain EM properties. Multiple follow-up papers have already replicated EM with non-coding tasks. The specific suggestion of misleading product reviews is a minor variant of what has already been tested across many domains. The core question — does EM generalize beyond code — has been answered affirmatively.
